source_checks.notes: Reachable via curl with declared UA (arstechnica CDN, PDF, 3.6MB). Confirmed by pdftotext: this is the actual filed appeal document (NAACP + Young, Gifted & Green, to the Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board), not a news article about it, so doc_type_ok=true and tier_assigned=1 (court/administrative filing category) is retained. Two caveats that keep the dependent entities at publish_flagged rather than publish: (1) it is hosted on a news outlet's CDN, not the Board's own site or a court record system - the Board apparently does not publish an online docket, and the underlying SCHD permit itself (01156-01PC) could not be independently retrieved (already in the analyst's gaps[]); (2) the claim that the Paul R. Lowry Road site and CTC Property LLC's turbines belong to 'xAI' is the appellants' own characterization inside an adversarial pleading, not a finding by the Health Department or an admission by xAI/CTC - the permit itself is issued to CTC Property LLC, not to any xAI-named entity. Document is dated July 16, 2025 on its face (line 1); research file records document_date 2025-07-15 (matches the filename '7-15-2025' and is within the few-day tolerance) - date_ok=true, noted here for the record.

Reachable via curl (TCEQ records.tceq.texas.gov), PDF confirmed genuine TCEQ Standard Permit Technical Review for 'Abilene DC 1, LLC dba Crusoe Energy Systems, LLC' / 'Longhorn Data Center'. summary:
Reviewed all 31 sources, all 223 evidence items, and issued verdicts for all 82 entities (25 companies, 20 facilities, 20 flows, 17 financial_links; 0 controls in this layer). Result: 68 publish, 14 publish_flagged, 0 reject. Every quote in the file was checked against the primary document: SEC filings via EDGAR full-text search (https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index, restricted to the filer's CIK/accession) since sec.gov blocks direct scripted fetches of the filing HTML itself; all other documents (company/gov press releases, NRC construction permit, TCEQ permit review, LPSC order, PJM/ERCOT filings, Siemens Energy annual report, the NAACP/YGG appeal) were downloaded directly with a declared project User-Agent and converted with pdftotext where needed. No fabricated or paraphrased quote was found anywhere in the file - every evidence item verified verbatim in the cited document, restricted to the correct filing/accession where relevant. This is an unusually clean research file; the issues found are about presentation/context rather than fabrication:

1. xAI Memphis (co:xai, fac:xai-colossus-turbines-memphis, flow:colossus-turbines-to-xai): the sole source is an appeal filed by NAACP and Young, Gifted & Green with the Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board, mirrored on a news outlet's CDN rather than the Board's own site. It is a genuine quasi-judicial filing (not press coverage), so I kept it Tier 1, but the claim that the Paul R. Lowry Road turbines are 'xAI's' is the appellants' own adversarial characterization - the permit itself names only CTC Property LLC. The flow was already correctly marked basis=inferred with a sound inference_note; I kept that and issued publish_flagged for all three dependent entities rather than reject, since the quoted facts (permit number, permit holder, turbine count) are accurately drawn from a real filing.

2. Abilene/Stargate (fac:crusoe-abilene-longhorn-turbines, flow:longhorn-turbines-to-oracle-stargate): the TCEQ permit for Crusoe's 'Longhorn Data Center' never mentions Stargate or Oracle, and Crusoe's own Stargate releases never use the name 'Longhorn'. The analyst's inference_note honestly states this gap. Facility-level facts (existence, operator, location, turbine counts) are solid Tier 1 TCEQ evidence and get publish; only the Oracle-directed flow, which depends on the Longhorn=Stargate identification, is publish_flagged.

3. Vistra MW figures (fac:vistra-perry, fac:vistra-davis-besse, fac:vistra-beaver-valley): capacity fields are the MW contracted to Meta under the 8-K PPA, not plant nameplate capacity. The analyst's own capacity.note already discloses this; I flagged all three publish_flagged so the caveat stays visible rather than relying on a reader opening the note.

4. Entergy Franklin Farms (fac:entergy-franklin-farms): the 2,262 MW capacity value is the LPSC-filed total for three CCCTs (Franklin Farms Units 1-2 plus the separately-modeled Waterford 5 facility), attached to a 2-unit facility entity; flagged for the same reason as the Vistra plants. Two Entergy financial_links (fin:meta-entergy-louisiana-esa, fin:meta-evest-entergy-esa) similarly carry Entergy's own capex estimates in their 'amount' field, not payment amounts - both already self-disclosed via note and flagged here for visibility.

5. Crane loan maturity (fin:doe-constellation-crane-loan): checked specifically for this review. Constellation's 10-K and its 10-Qs give different maturity months (October 2055 vs. November 2055, confirmed present in different 2026 filings via EDGAR full-text search); the research file's description says only 'matures 2055' with no month, so it cannot assert the wrong one. No correction needed; verdict publish.

6. Talen-Amazon value (fin:amazon-talen-susquehanna-ppa): confirmed no amount field is present and the description correctly states the ~$18B figure reported in the press does not appear in the cited 8-K exhibit. No correction needed.

7. FERC ER24-2172 (flow:susquehanna-to-amazon): the underlying facts (PJM/PPL/Susquehanna ISA amendment for up to 480 MW of co-located AWS supply, denied by FERC in November 2024) are verified verbatim in Talen's 10-K. The specific docket number 'ER24-2172' that the flow's description adds is not itself present in that 10-K text (EDGAR full-text search returns zero hits for it in Talen's filings); FERC.gov and eLibrary block scripted access, matching the analyst's own gaps[] entry, so I could not independently confirm the docket number against FERC's own record. It matches the citation the analyst separately records in gaps[] (189 FERC P 61,078, Nov. 1, 2024) and public reporting on this case, so I left it in place with a note rather than removing it; it doesn't affect any verified numeric claim. I found no assertion anywhere in the file about Talen dropping an appeal in January 2026 (a fact flagged for me to check) - the data makes no such claim, so there is nothing to correct.

8. Entergy's pending March 2026 filing (fac:entergy-richland-parish-units-1-4, fac:entergy-pointe-coupee-units-1-3, flow:richland-units-to-meta, flow:pointe-coupee-units-to-meta): correctly described throughout as 'planned'/'pending' (Evest LLC, 5,278 MW, $12.9B, 'application is pending before the LPSC' per the 10-Q) and never as approved, unlike the already-decided Order U-37425 (2,262 MW, Laidley LLC, decided at the LPSC's August 20, 2025 session). Flagged publish_flagged purely to keep the pending status visible; no correction needed.

9. Systemic note (not a rejection): company hq coordinates are explicitly evidenced for only 5 of 25 companies (X-energy, GE Vernova, Dominion, WEC Energy, NiSource - all from SEC cover pages or explicit hq quotes). The other 20 rely on general knowledge of well-known corporate addresses at 'city' or coarser precision, which AGENTS.md's coordinate rule permits (documented address is required only at 'site' precision). I did not reject or flag these individually; co:xai is flagged separately above on other grounds and additionally has no hq evidence at all.

No entity was rejected. No fabricated quotes, no paraphrases presented as quotes, and no 'documented' flow found that should actually be 'inferred' (the two flows that needed basis=inferred - xAI/Memphis and Longhorn/Stargate - were already correctly marked that way by the analyst).
